name: VEML6070 UV light sensor
description: Vishay UVA light sensor (peak 355 nm, 320-410 nm) with a 16-bit reading over I2C. It has no register pointer: commands are written to 0x38, the reading is read as MSB from 0x39 and LSB from 0x38, and 0x0C is the alert response address. Chip supply 2.7-5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit VEML6070 UV Index Sensor Breakout (#2899), 5-pin header VIN, G, SCL, SDA, ACK with 10k pull-ups on SCL, SDA and ACK and a 270k RSET (no regulator).
eli5: Measures how strong the sun's ultraviolet light is, so you can tell when you need sunscreen.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3-5 V, goes straight to the chip (no regulator); the I2C and ACK pull-ups go to this voltage, so use 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10k pull-up to VIN on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10k pull-up to VIN on the board)

pins.name: ACK
pins.description: Alert output, open-drain with a 10k pull-up to VIN: goes low when the UV reading passes the ACK threshold (if enabled); not needed for basic use

supplierQuery: VEML6070 UV light sensor breakout I2C
buildNotes: Initialise within 150 ms of power-up: read the alert response address 0x0C once (clears any ACK alert; the chip may NACK it when none is pending), then write the command 0x06 to 0x38 (IT = 1T, running).
Read the 16-bit result as two single-byte reads: MSB from 0x39, then LSB from 0x38. Never write to 0x39.
The refresh time is set by RSET: 125 ms at 1T with 300k (datasheet table 4); the Adafruit board's 270k gives about 113-126 ms. Wait one refresh after a command before reading.
UV risk bands at 1T / 270k (Vishay app note 84310): 0-560 low, 561-1120 moderate, 1121-1494 high, 1495-2054 very high, 2055+ extreme. Divide the reading by 2 or 4 at 2T / 4T first.
The chip answers at 0x38, 0x39 and 0x0C, so nothing else on the bus may use those addresses (0x38 clashes with AHT10/AHT20 sensors and some PCF8574A boards).
VIN also powers the 10k pull-ups, so power the board from 3.3 V when using a 3.3 V microcontroller.
Behind glass or plastic the reading drops a lot: most window materials block UV. Test it outdoors in sunlight.

driver.code:
# VEML6070 UVA light sensor (Vishay datasheet doc 84277), MicroPython driver.
# The chip has no register pointer. It answers at three I2C addresses:
#   0x38  write: the 8-bit command register; read: UV data LSB
#   0x39  read: UV data MSB (never write to 0x39)
#   0x0C  alert response address (ARA): reading it clears a pending ACK alert
# Command byte: bit5 ACK enable, bit4 ACK_THD (0 = 102, 1 = 145 steps),
# bits3:2 IT (0 = 1/2T, 1 = 1T, 2 = 2T, 3 = 4T), bit1 reserved = 1, bit0 SD (1 = shutdown).
# Initialisation per datasheet: clear the ACK state, then write 0x06 (IT = 1T, running).
import time

_ADDR_CMD_LSB = 0x38
_ADDR_MSB = 0x39
_ADDR_ARA = 0x0C

IT_HALF = 0
IT_1 = 1
IT_2 = 2
IT_4 = 4
_IT_BITS = {IT_HALF: 0, IT_1: 1, IT_2: 2, IT_4: 3}

# UV risk bands in steps at IT = 1T with RSET = 270 k (Vishay app note 84310, as used
# by Adafruit's library). Scale the reading to 1T before comparing.
_RISK = ((560, 'LOW'), (1120, 'MODERATE'), (1494, 'HIGH'), (2054, 'VERY HIGH'))


class VEML6070:
    def __init__(self, i2c, it=IT_1, rset_kohm=270):
        if it not in _IT_BITS:
            raise ValueError('it must be IT_HALF, IT_1, IT_2 or IT_4')
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.it = it
        # 1T refresh time scales with RSET: 125 ms at 300 k (datasheet table 4);
        # Adafruit measured about 126 ms on its 270 k board, so add 10 % margin.
        self._t1_ms = max(125, rset_kohm * 125 // 300) * 11 // 10
        self.clear_ack()
        self._cmd = (_IT_BITS[it] << 2) | 0x02  # ACK off, SD = 0 (running)
        self._write()
        self.wait()

    def _write(self):
        self.i2c.writeto(_ADDR_CMD_LSB, bytes([self._cmd]))

    def clear_ack(self):
        """Read the alert response address; returns True if an alert was pending."""
        try:
            self.i2c.readfrom(_ADDR_ARA, 1)
            return True
        except OSError:
            return False  # no alert pending: the chip does not answer at 0x0C

    def wait(self):
        """Sleep one refresh period of the current integration time."""
        t = self._t1_ms // 2 if self.it == IT_HALF else self._t1_ms * self.it
        time.sleep_ms(t + 5)

    def raw(self):
        """UV reading in steps (0..65535): MSB from 0x39, then LSB from 0x38."""
        msb = self.i2c.readfrom(_ADDR_MSB, 1)[0]
        lsb = self.i2c.readfrom(_ADDR_CMD_LSB, 1)[0]
        return (msb << 8) | lsb

    def risk(self, steps=None):
        """UV risk level (LOW .. EXTREME) from the app note bands; not for IT_HALF."""
        if self.it == IT_HALF:
            raise ValueError('risk bands are defined for IT_1, IT_2 and IT_4 only')
        if steps is None:
            steps = self.raw()
        s = steps // self.it
        for top, name in _RISK:
            if s <= top:
                return name
        return 'EXTREME'

    def set_ack(self, enable=True, threshold_145=False):
        """Enable the ACK pin alert when the reading exceeds 102 (or 145) steps."""
        self._cmd = (self._cmd & ~0x30) | (0x20 if enable else 0) | (0x10 if threshold_145 else 0)
        self.clear_ack()
        self._write()

    def sleep(self, off=True):
        """Shutdown mode (about 1 uA). off=False starts measuring again."""
        self._cmd = (self._cmd | 0x01) if off else (self._cmd & ~0x01)
        self._write()
        if not off:
            self.wait()

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from veml6070 import VEML6070, IT_1

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
uv = VEML6070(i2c, it=IT_1)  # 1T: about 125 ms per reading with the board's 270k RSET
while True:
    steps = uv.raw()
    print('UV=%d risk=%s' % (steps, uv.risk(steps)))
    time.sleep(1)
